{{Short description|Message authentication code algorithm}}
{{More citations needed|date=December 2019}}
'''PMAC''', which stands for '''parallelizable MAC''', is a [[message authentication code]] algorithm.  It was created by [[Phillip Rogaway]].
PMAC is a method of taking a [[block cipher]] and creating an efficient message authentication code that is reducible in security to the underlying block cipher.

PMAC is similar in functionality to the [[OMAC (cryptography)|OMAC]] algorithm.

==Patents==
PMAC is no longer patented and can be used royalty-free. It was originally patented by [[Phillip Rogaway]], but he has since abandoned his patent filings.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://web.cs.ucdavis.edu/~rogaway/ocb/pmac-bak.htm |title=PMAC – A Parallelizable MAC – Background|last=Rogaway|first=Phillip|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>
